describe_dataset.description: Read how MANTO is put together: every record type it publishes and the fields each one carries, with the IDs Search any record type takes. Run it once to learn which field names the other actions will hand back before building on them. No account or API key required.

mock_response.citation: MANTO, edited by Greta Hawes and R. Scott Smith, https://www.manto-myth.org/manto

find_entities_near.description: Find the places, landmarks and other entities MANTO locates within a distance of a point on the map, nearest first, each with how far away it is. Give the latitude and longitude of a site, a museum or a tour stop and see which myths are set there; limit it to one kind, such as landmarks, if you like. No account or API key required.

parameters.description: The latitude of the point to search around, in degrees north, such as 37.9715 for Athens. A place's latitude from an earlier step works.

parameters.name: longitude

get_entities.description: Read several entities' records in one step, in the order you gave them, with the same detail as Get an entity. get_entity.description: Read one entity's whole record: its name and kind, every field, every record it points at, where MANTO places it, and every tie the ancient sources record on it, with the stable address to cite. Give the MANTO ID, the stable address or the public page; a link copied from anywhere on MANTO works. No account or API key required.

get_entity_connections.description: List every tie that names an entity: the assertions the ancient passages and artifacts make about it, such as whose child it is, where it was born, what it founded, who killed it, each as a sentence with the source that makes it, the part the entity plays and the records it points at. The links come back as MANTO IDs, so a workflow can hand them straight to Get several entities and walk the storyworld a step at a time. No account or API key required.

search_entities.description: Find the gods, heroes, monsters, collectives, places, landmarks, objects, events and constellations of Greek myth by name, of every kind or of one. Each result carries its kind, its fields, the records it points at, where MANTO places it, how many ties name it and the stable address to cite, and the ID to hand to Get an entity for the whole story. No account or API key required.
search_entities.name: search_entities

parameters.description: A name or part of one. MANTO's names mix Greek and Latin spellings (Medousa and Dionysos, but Achilles and Heracles), and the search allows near spellings, so Medusa still finds Medousa; when a search comes back empty, try the other spelling. Part of a name is enough: Dion finds Dionysos and Dione.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Turn this on to keep only the entities whose own name holds every word. Left off, alternative names count too and near spellings are allowed, so Zeus also finds the Rock of Theseus, once called the Altar of Zeus. With it on, a page can hold fewer than the page size; keep paging to see every match.

search_records.description: Search or page through any record type MANTO publishes, not only its entities: its ties (every assertion, such as Perseus kills Medousa), the passages, texts and authors they come from, the artifacts that depict them and the vocabularies they use. description: Look up the people, places and stories of Greek myth in MANTO, the linked open dataset of Greek mythology built by Greta Hawes and R. Scott Smith: more than 9,000 entities, among them some 5,300 gods, heroes, monsters and animals, the collectives they belong to, the places, landmarks and objects of the storyworld, its events and its constellations, tied together by some 34,000 assertions from the ancient texts and artifacts, each with a stable address to cite. Search by name or kind, find what is set near a point on the map, read an entity and every tie that names it, page through the whole dataset, or read how it is put together. No account or API key required.
